**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/20 (Sat) 18:25  
[FACT] User is inquiring about USB ports on a Raspberry Pi running Android OS.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] USB ports on a Raspberry Pi running Android are enumerated like any other computer running Android, with the OS assigning a unique device number and device class to connected devices.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The `lsusb` command can be used in a terminal window to list the device number, device class, and manufacturer for each USB device connected to the system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Android Device Manager tool can also be used to view information about USB devices connected to the Raspberry Pi.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To access the Device Manager, go to the Settings app, select "About phone" or "About tablet," and then select "Hardware information" or "Device information."  
[USER] User wants to power off one of the USB ports but is unsure how to identify which one corresponds to a particular device.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To power off a particular USB port, the `echo` command can be used to write the value "0" to the appropriate sysfs file for that port.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Example command to power off the USB port associated with device number 3: `echo 0 > /sys/devices/platform/soc/3c980000.usb/buspower`.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] This command will only power off the USB port and will not physically disconnect the device from the port; the device must be unplugged to physically disconnect it.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Not all Raspberry Pi models and configurations support the ability to power off individual USB ports; if unable to power off a port, it may not be supported on the user's system.
